# Camera

<!-- Generated by `python3 scripts/pick.py --write-docs references` from assets/library/techniques.json. Edit the JSON, then regenerate. -->

Pushes, drifts, reframes, parallax, holds that creep and moves that accelerate into the cut. 49 entries, by category and role. The [index](../technique-library.md) lists every family and each category's house rule.

### Shot opens already moving

`dv-opens-already-moving` · opening hooks · workhorse · energy medium · any

The first frame of a film or a shot already carries a lateral drift, a pan at full speed or a decelerating push (a third of the travel in the first 10 % of the move), which settles on the subject.

- **Build:** handoffShot()/carriedCut() for cuts; for the opener, a move on E.snapOut whose first frame is already partway. Anatomy: Pan 126 px/f decaying, or a push x1.43 with 36 % of the zoom in the first tenth, or a drift of 12.9 px/f plus a slow zoom-out that decays. Sound: The first music hit at about 0.15 s.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Settle 36-80 f, front-loaded; critically damped.
- **Use when:** The film's first frame; every shot after a transition.
- **Avoid when:** Starting from a parked frame (it reads as a slideshow).

### Asymmetric whip: long build, short brake

`dv-asymmetric-whip` · camera · workhorse · energy high · any

A fast reframe whose speed builds for most of the move and brakes in the last third, crisp at the peak (no blur needed below about 100 px/f at 1080p); the copy swaps inside the peak frames.

- **Build:** whip({ frames: 32 }) + swapAt(whip.peak). Anatomy: Build 60-70 % of the move, brake 30-40 %; a slight zoom-out rides along; placeholder -> typed swap at the peak; a second, faster whip can follow immediately. Sound: A pop or a pluck at the peak (within 30 ms).
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 23-69 f; peak 50-178 px/f at 63-70 % of the move; house 32 f, peak 1600 px/s.
- **Use when:** Changing subject inside one shot; racing up or down a phone; tilting into darkness.
- **Avoid when:** Symmetric eases (they read as a slide).

### Camera follows the caret

`dv-caret-follow` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough

While text types in a field cropped by the frame, the camera pans with the caret (in pulses, starting a few frames before the typing), and may pull back in one frame to show the whole field when the line ends.

- **Build:** typeSchedule() positions -> a camera x with a short lead; the jump-out as a HardStep on the framing. Anatomy: Pan speed 1-40 px/f tracking the caret; the pan starts 7 f before the typing; a one-frame jump-out at the end; a decaying roll drift while the next label types. Sound: Spacebar presses.
- **Primitive:** `fx/TypeOn`
- **Timing:** Over the typing (50-145 f); jump-out 1 f; settle 32 f.
- **Use when:** Typing in close-up.
- **Avoid when:** Following every character exactly (lead it slightly).

### Camera reframes to make room

`dv-make-room-reframe` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · any

When a new element is about to arrive, the camera (or the content) pulls back, shrinks or slides to make room, timed to finish one frame before the new element shows; a push can stay centred on an inline icon so the words part around it.

- **Build:** A camera move ending at the new element's onset - 1 (whip or E.glideOut); for an icon-centred push, anchor = the icon. Anatomy: Pull-back to 0.69-0.75; a kick of -6.3 %/f at peak; a 368 px slide with an early speed peak (18 % of the move) and a long tail; a two-phase pull (decelerate, re-accelerate, settle). Sound: A kick or a click. Materials: When the cluster outgrows the panel, the whole composition shrinks about 18 % between two drawings with no in-betweens (no blur, no overshoot), paired with a new tile's cut-on, and the slow pan continues.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Materials:** When the cluster outgrows the panel, the whole composition shrinks about 18 % between two drawings with no in-betweens (no blur, no overshoot), paired with a new tile's cut-on, and the slow pan continues.
- **Timing:** 30-60 f; peak at 18-56 % of the move.
- **Use when:** Adding a second line, more cards, a label, a result under a search bar.
- **Avoid when:** Making room after the element has appeared.

### Chained reframes with a pulse

`cam-chained-reframes` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · feature, launch, loop · also `dv-reframe-chain`

The camera tours the product in S-curved moves; each move swells a few percent in scale at its fastest moment and leans with a little roll, and between moves the frame keeps drifting.

- **Build:** reframeChain([A, B, C], { start, frames, gap, ease, rollEase, pulse, residual, fps }) returns the camera for any frame and .moves. Give each framing its own roll (3-8 deg of change per move) and an arrive curve that overshoots 1-2 % as rollEase. Land each move as the cursor or the next element reaches its target.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.reframeChain`
- **Timing:** Moves 48 f on E.strongInOut (27-126 f), peak 1600-5000 px/s at 45-55 % of the move; scale pulse +5 % at peak speed settling to +1 %; near-holds 8 f (4-12 f) drifting 30 px/s.
- **Use when:** A product tour, a board of features, one camera journey.
- **Avoid when:** The product must be read (forms, tables): hold still there.

### Copy swap on a push's fastest frame

`cam-swap-on-push-peak` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature · also `dv-copy-swap-on-peak`

A push carries the board toward the viewer; on its fastest frame the line changes. The mirrored pull-back swaps again on its own peak, through one empty frame.

- **Build:** Run the push and the pull as two eased log-scale moves (whip() between two framings at different k, or lmix on any curve). peakFrame(ease, start, frames) is each move's fastest whole frame. On the push: swapAt(peak, { lead: 1 }); on the pull: swapAt(peak, { lead: 0, blank: 1 }).
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.peakFrame`, `lib/camera-moves.swapAt`
- **Timing:** Push x1.4 over 27 f@30 on a strong in-out, pull back past the start (x0.92) over 35 f@30; the push's peak is about 0.045 ln-scale per frame. New copy 35-40 % on its first frame, 0.9 by 8 frames later.
- **Use when:** A statement in two parts over a board of product cards.
- **Avoid when:** The copy is long: one or two words swap well, a sentence does not.

### Detail first, then pull back

`cam-detail-first-pullback` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, walkthrough

A shot opens tight on the one thing that matters (giant prompt words, a chart counting up, a status pill) with no chrome, then the camera pulls back to show it sitting in the full window.

- **Build:** Anchor on the hero element (ax, ay at its centre, or at the caret for typed words) and hold k = 1.6-1.7 while its value animates; for giant type, pan sx after the caret at 2-4 px/f. Then pull with cam = lc(TIGHT, CONTEXT, prog(f, a, a + 52, E.cam)), so the hero barely moves on screen while the frame widens around it, and fade out any partly cropped edge tiles over the 16 f before the pull so they don't pop at the frame edge. Bring the context in during the pull: window chrome and neighbouring panels fade 0 -> 1 over 30 f from 20% of the move, optionally behind <RackFocus t={1 - prog(f, a, a + 30, E.smooth)} blur={10}>. The hero card can tip pitch 0 -> 6 -> 0 deg and yaw 0 -> -4 -> 0 deg as it docks into its slot. For an end-of-film re-establish, open the tight frame soft (RackFocus t = 1, blur 6) and resolve it over the pull.
- **Timing:** Tight hold 24-52 f while the value animates. Pull k 1.6-1.7 -> 1.0 over 52 f on E.cam (peak about 4%/f at 27%), or a settle back over 56-80 f on E.out (half done by f10-12). Edge tiles out over 16 f before the pull, context in over 30 f, 3D tip peaking mid-move. Re-establish k 2.2 -> 1.0 with focus over 60 f on E.cam (peak about 5.6%/f).
- **Use when:** Result reveals, analytics, prompts and input moments where the value should land before the load of the full UI; breaking up a repeated card formula; re-establishing the whole product after a run of close details.
- **Avoid when:** The product hasn't been seen yet and the tight frame stays unrecognisable for long (keep the tight hold under 52 f), or the wider frame adds nothing new.

### Every cut breathes

`cam-scale-breath-cut` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · launch, feature, loop, vertical · also `dv-cut-open-big-settle`

The outgoing shot pushes in a few percent, faster and faster, and cuts on its fastest frame; the incoming shot opens a little too big and settles, so the cut reads as one continuous breath instead of a jump.

- **Build:** Wrap the two framings in scaleBreath({ from, to, cut, fps }) and draw every frame through camera(shot). The push into the cut is built like a launch (the step k frames before the cut is exp(-a * s^p) of the cut step; pass build, or a and p, or explicit growth ratios). After the cut the incoming shot opens off its rest by post.open and settles on post.ease. mode 'flip' (house) opens big and settles down; 'same' opens small and keeps pushing in. breathK(f, opts) is the multiplier alone for a camera you already have.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.scaleBreath`
- **Timing:** Push 3 % into the cut over 20 f (normal 1-8 % over 10-20 f), the last frame the fastest. Next shot opens 8 % off (normal 5-12 %) and settles in 30 f on E.glideOut (8-50 f). A strong breath for an act break: open 14 % and settle in about 1 s on a front-loaded ease.
- **Use when:** Any hard cut between two shots of the same film; the default for every cut that has no other device.
- **Avoid when:** The cut is a designed hard stop on a hit with a freeze (keep that one still).

### Fit-to-content follow

`cam-fit-bounds-follow` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

As a route, graph or plan builds, the camera widens just enough to keep every piece that matters in frame, so the shot opens close on the first node and ends on the whole structure.

- **Build:** Each frame, collect the world boxes that must stay visible: the origin, every item revealed so far (with its half-size) and the travelling head if there is one, its box stretched ahead along its direction of travel by 18% of the frame converted to world px at the current k. Turn their bounding box plus a 12% frame margin into a target shot: ax, ay at the box centre, sx, sy at frame centre (or shifted off the caption band), and k = min((W - 2 x SAFE.x) / boxW, (H - 2 x SAFE.y) / boxH), clamped between the opening k and a floor that keeps the smallest label at TYPE.ui size (24 px) on screen; when the floor binds, let the oldest items leave the frame rather than shrinking type. Smooth it as a pure function of the frame: loop i from the shot's first frame to f, keep lnT = min(lnT, ln kTarget(i)) so the zoom never pumps back in while the set grows, and step c += (target - c) x 0.07 for ax, ay and ln k, clamping each step to 1.2% of zoom and 12 px of screen travel, then feed exp(c.lnk) to the anchor camera so the widening keeps an even pace in log space. When the structure is complete, either hold the full fit as the payoff under a cam-living-hold pull or punch in on the destination with lc(FOLLOW, DEST, prog(f, e, e + 54, E.cam)).
- **Timing:** Follow coefficient 0.06-0.08 per frame (time constant 12-16 f); zoom at most 1.2%/f, centre at most 12 px/f on screen (--blur if the corners ever pass 12 px/f). Margin 12% of the frame, 18% lead on the head's side. Nodes 20-40 f apart give a steady widening rather than steps. Closing punch-in 48-60 f on E.cam, or a hold with a -0.08%/f pull.
- **Use when:** Pipelines, agent plans, org charts, dependency or network graphs and routes that build piece by piece, where the first node needs close-up legibility and the payoff is the whole shape.
- **Avoid when:** The finished structure already fits one comfortable framing, a single moving lead is the whole story (cam-lead-follow), or the full structure cannot fit with 24 px labels (split it into chapters with cuts instead).

### Follow the lead dot

`cam-lead-follow` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, vertical, launch

A small lead (a progress dot, a travelling packet, a drawing line's head) moves through the layout and the camera follows it with a soft lag, never quite stopping, so the viewer always knows where to look.

- **Build:** Make the follow a pure function of the frame: loop i from the shot's first frame to f, updating c += (lead(i) - target - c) * 0.08 (target is the lead's desired screen position, for example 40% of the frame height), plus a constant 2 px/f drift in the direction of travel; never keep state between renders. Feed c into the anchor camera (ax, ay on the lead's world point) and draw the lead as a flat dot in the one accent colour with no halo. Reveal each step row as the lead passes it: opacity prog(f, tPass, tPass + 12, E.smooth) with a 12 px rise through arrive(). At a corner, let the lead turn first and the camera's lag carry the turn; at the destination, punch in (cam-punch-in-insert) or ease to rest on E.rest.
- **Timing:** Lag coefficient 0.08 per frame (time constant about 12 f). Peak 12.5 px/f, residual drift 2-2.5 px/f, never 0. Step rows reveal over 12 f as the lead passes. Bumps between steps about 40 f.
- **Use when:** Agent progress, pipelines, timelines and journeys across a map: any story told by one thing moving through a layout.
- **Avoid when:** The lead moves faster than about 20 px/f for long stretches (the lag lets it escape the frame), or the whole layout fits in one framing.

### Isolating push into one item

`cam-isolating-push` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch

The camera pushes into one row, card or column while everything around it fades, dims or slides off the edges, picking a single thread out of a busy layout.

- **Build:** Anchor the push on the chosen item and pick a preset. Dive: k x lmix(1, 4, prog(f, a, a + 80, E.smooth)) while sibling rows fade from 1 to 0 opacity over 20 f from a; as the push ends, the item's icon dims to 0.3 and the next state swaps in on a whole frame (fd), a zoom-through without a cut. Accelerate-through: k x lmix(1, 1.25, prog(f, a, a + 60, E.in)) while the surroundings fade to the background colour over 16 f, then cut or swap on the peak frame. Eject: k x lmix(1, 1.48, prog(f, a, a + 30, E.smooth)) and then +4% over 60 f on E.linear, the flanking words taking blurOut text blur up to 6 px once they pass 80% of the half-width on their way off frame. Gentle focus: wrap the side columns in RackFocus (t 0 -> 1, blur 8) and dim them to 0.6 opacity while the parent pushes x1.06 over 18 f on E.smooth.
- **Timing:** Dive 80 f, x4 on E.smooth (peak about 5%/f), sibling fades 20 f, swap on the last frame. Accelerate-through 60 f, x1.25 on E.in, surround fade 16 f. Eject 30 f, x1.48 on E.smooth, then +4% over 60 f. Focus pull 18 f, x1.06, blur 8 px, opacity 0.6, running straight into the next move.
- **Use when:** Choosing one result from a list of parallel processes, moving from a typographic act into a UI close-up without a cut, or steering the eye to where the next action will happen.
- **Avoid when:** The item is still too small to read at 4x, or the surrounding layout carries information the viewer still needs.

### Layered parallax push or truck

`cam-parallax-truck` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

One camera move seen by two or three depth planes: the type moves with the camera, the cards behind at about half its rate, the ground not at all, so a flat layout reads as space.

- **Build:** parallax([{ w: 1 }, { w: 0.55 }, { w: 0 }], { from, to, start, frames, ease }) returns the framings of the layers for frame f (each layer scales by exp(w * ln(k / k0)) around the same anchor, takes pan = w of the pan, may start lag frames late and ride its own curve). Draw each layer as its own sibling world, never a child transform. For a stepped look feed the move stepFrame(f, { animFps: 16 }) and declare the range in STEPPED.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.parallax`
- **Timing:** Push x1.16 on the type over 14-18 f@24 (tiles x1.08: weight about 0.55), or a truck of 200-400 px over 90-120 f on E.liftOut with plane factors 0.3 / 1.0 / 1.6; background overscan 5-8 %.
- **Use when:** Hero product shots and feature cards that need depth without 3D, and slow establishing moves.
- **Avoid when:** Dense UI walkthroughs where the eye has to track one control, or any scene with more than three planes (it starts to look like a parallax demo).

### Long exponential camera settle

`dv-long-decay-settle` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · any

One long move that decays exponentially over 1-2.5 s (a pull-back of 15 %, a 357 px slide, a layout easing out to 0.88, a push of 1.21x on a finished line), settling just before the next beat; it can start with a tiny anticipation push.

- **Build:** A move on E.glideOut (or a decayEase) between two framings; anticipation via reversal with a short pull. Anatomy: Quint- or circ-out; t50 about 0.12-0.2 s, t90 about 0.6 s; optional +0.8 % push before a pull-back. Sound: The bed; the next beat lands on the settle.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 46-160 f; tau about 48 f.
- **Use when:** Calm shots after a busy one; holds on photos and dashboards.
- **Avoid when:** Ending the settle after the next cut (then it is not a settle).

### Move accelerates into the cut

`dv-accelerate-into-cut` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · any

The shot leaves by speeding up (a drift, a push, a pull-back, a card shrinking away) and the cut lands on its fastest frame; even a slow push that would normally settle keeps rising into the cut.

- **Build:** scaleBreath (push into .cut) or punchOut; put the cut on .cut / peakFrame. Anatomy: Ease-in over the last 6-24 f; a held line growing 0.18 %/f then +3.2 % in its last 6 f; a 3-frame counter-move (0.997, 0.990, 0.976) after a slow push. Sound: Kick 24 ms after the cut; a riser or a level swell into it; a spoken word on the cut.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Last 6-70 f on an ease-in; cut speed 6-30 px/f or 0.4-1.5 %/f.
- **Use when:** Nearly every cut; the end of a film (the last frame at peak speed).
- **Avoid when:** Settling into the cut (that reads as a stall).

### Pull-back that lands an event

`cam-pull-lands-event` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

A long, gentle pull-back runs from a close-up to the full view, and as it decelerates the next UI event (a modal, labels, a caption) starts, so it lands together with the camera's settle.

- **Build:** Pull with lc(CLOSE, WIDE, prog(f, a, a + 108, E.smooth)), where WIDE.k is about 0.56 x CLOSE.k. Start the event at a + round(0.72 x 108) = a + 78. A modal arrives on SPR.firm from 0.92 to 1 scale, opacity up over 8 f, landing within 4 f of a + 108. Captions start no earlier than a + 81 (the last 25% of the move) and no later than a + 114, while labels and values can type in through the whole pull. After the settle, hand over to a breath creep instead of a dead lock.
- **Timing:** 108 f on E.smooth, zoom x0.56, peak about 1.5%/f (about 24 px/f) mid-move. Event starts at 72% of the move; the SPR.firm modal settles within 4 f of the camera. Captions start in the last 25% of the move or up to 6 f after it.
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs and single-take films that move pose to pose, and any long move whose ending would otherwise be a dead beat.
- **Avoid when:** Short or fast moves under 50 f, where an event in the tail just competes with the motion, and the finale, where the lockup needs a clean frame.

### Punch-in insert on the same render

`cam-punch-in-insert` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · feature, walkthrough, launch, vertical

A hard cut jumps from the wide view to a 2-2.5x on-axis close-up, or to a 3-4.5x macro of the exact control being used, while every animation keeps running, then cuts back out.

- **Build:** Lay the product out once and define two Shots on it: WIDE, and INSERT with ax, ay on the control's centre (or the cursor tip), sx, sy at frame centre or on a third, and k = 2.0-2.5 for an on-axis punch or 3-4.5 for a macro insert. Switch on a whole frame, cam = fd(f) >= CUT ? INSERT : WIDE, and keep the cursor path, hover lift, typing and counters on their own clocks so they carry on mid-motion across the cut; place the cursor with toScreen() of the active shot. Never hold the insert still: give it a 1-2 px/f linear drift along the action's direction, or open it with a decaying offset (+8% of frame width, decayed on E.out over 96 f). Build the UI as live layout at its final size, never as an upscaled bitmap, so text stays sharp at k = 4.5, and cut back out on the next action or at the peak of an exit move.
- **Timing:** Wide holds 20-64 f before an on-axis punch (90-220 f when it establishes the scene). On-axis close-up about 60 f. Macro insert 46-74 f, up to 76-154 f when it carries an action. Scale 2.0-2.5 on-axis, 3-4.5 macro. Drift inside the insert 1-2 px/f linear (3-5 px/f for a 2.5x component slide). Cut on the click, keystroke or beat, with no transition frames. Chain 2-3 punches on consecutive beats for a staccato build.
- **Use when:** Small UI actions that need hero weight (send, picking a date, a chip), long walkthroughs that need their visual scale reset, and a wide/close rhythm that keeps both context and legibility.
- **Avoid when:** The UI doesn't hold up at 3-4.5x, or the close-up isn't obviously the same place (keep the cut on-axis or anchored to the cursor, or it reads as a jump).

### Punch-in zoom carried by a few frames

`dv-punch-in` · camera · workhorse · energy high · any

A zoom whose change happens in 1-3 explosive frames after a short creep, then an expo tail; punch-ins can be hidden on spoken words, and two punches in a row replace one push.

- **Build:** <SnapZoom to pre post defocus>. Anatomy: Creep (+0.04 -> +3.3 %/f), 1-3 big frames (x1.15, 1.38, 1.60), tail; x1.11-1.47 per punch; optional 5.6 px defocus on the jump frame and a 3 f ease-in before. Sound: On the spoken word (-10 ms) or the hit.
- **Primitive:** `fx/SnapZoom`
- **Timing:** 18-45 f in all; jump 1-3 f; tail 20-40 f.
- **Use when:** A hit, a label landing, the spoken key word.
- **Avoid when:** Every cut (save it for hits).

### Reactive reframe

`cam-reframe-to-subject` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

When something new appears (a popover, a result, the hero icon), the camera glides a few hundred pixels and pushes in slightly until it sits where the eye wants it.

- **Build:** On the event cue c, blend from the current camera into a reframed Shot: cam = lc(CURRENT, REFRAMED, prog(f, c + 4, c + 4 + N, E.glide)). REFRAMED puts ax, ay on the new element's centre and sx, sy at frame centre (or offset to leave room for its caption), with k = CURRENT.k x 1.05-1.23. Starting 4 f after the element begins to appear lets the content lead and the camera follow. The element arrives on its own curve; a popover, for example, scales 0.05 -> 1 from the click point over 10 f on E.out, its opacity rising over the first 4 f. To centre a hero after a punch-in, use the same blend over 22 f with position and k on one curve, so the subject arrives on a long tail.
- **Timing:** Popover reframe: starts 4 f after the pop, settles in 20-40 f on E.glide, k x1.05. Hero centring: 22 f on E.glide, 150-350 px of travel, peak about 22 px/f at 31% of the move, k 1.0 -> 1.23.
- **Use when:** After any UI event that changes what matters on screen, or after a punch-in that left the hero off-centre.
- **Avoid when:** Every small UI change (keep it for the ones that matter), or an element that already appears near frame centre (a move under 40 px reads as a twitch).

### Seamless loop drift

`cam-seamless-loop-orbit` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · loop, vertical

In a looping clip the camera drifts along a slow, closed figure-eight (a little sideways, a little up, breathing in and out) and returns exactly to its first frame, so the loop has no seam.

- **Build:** With L the loop length in frames and u = 2 * Math.PI * f / L, set sx = sx0 + 32 * Math.sin(u), sy = sy0 + 12 * Math.sin(2 * u) and k = k0 * Math.exp(0.03 * Math.sin(u + 1.2)) on the anchor camera, plus yaw = 3 * Math.sin(u) deg for a 3D product. Every term completes a whole number of cycles in L, so frame L equals frame 0 exactly and the motion never stops (the speed peaks around 0.6 px/f at L = 360). Time the content's own loop to L or a divisor of it.
- **Timing:** Loop L = 240-480 f. Amplitudes 24-40 px sideways and 10-16 px vertically (at twice the frequency), zoom +-3%, yaw +-3 deg. Peak speed about 0.5-0.8 px/f.
- **Use when:** Feature loops, background clips and vertical loops that replay endlessly.
- **Avoid when:** Linear films with cuts (use a living hold instead), or loops shorter than about 4 s, where the drift turns into a visible wobble.

### The camera operates a flat UI

`dv-flat-ui-camera` · camera · workhorse · energy calm · feature, walkthrough

The real app UI is never animated as layers: the camera zooms out, scrolls and pushes over one flat canvas, so the product looks untouched and the editing does the talking.

- **Build:** One camera() on a single flat <Img> or built canvas; moves from lib/camera-moves. Anatomy: Zooms x0.70-0.92 and scrolls 94-551 px; a symmetric 1.33x zoom; an S-curve push of +30 % on a finished layout. Sound: Voice.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Zooms 30-40 f; calm scroll+zoom 75 f; S-push 92 f.
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs of a real product from screenshots.
- **Avoid when:** Fake layer animation on a screenshot.

### Zoom-out hop between areas

`cam-zoom-out-hop` · camera · workhorse · energy medium · walkthrough, feature, launch

To travel between two distant parts of one product, the camera eases back as it sets off, crosses at a wider framing that shows where it is going, and pushes back in as it arrives.

- **Build:** Keyframe Shots A and B at the same k on the two areas, blend cam = lc(A, B, prog(f, a, a + N, E.smooth)), then multiply cam.k by dip(prog(f, a, a + N, E.linear), depth) from src/lib/camera.ts. Driving the dip on linear time instead of on the pan's eased progress is the point: the pull-back starts before the pan gathers speed and the push-in finishes after it slows, so the widest framing coincides with the fastest travel and the frame edge peaks 28-40% lower than the same pan without the hop. Set depth = clamp(1 - 0.7 x W / (A.k x D), 0.15, 0.45), where D is the world distance between the anchors, so both areas share the frame at mid-move, and size N = A.k x D / 34 frames at depth 0.45 (A.k x D / 25 for a shallow 0.15-0.25 hop, interpolated between) to keep the edge under about 60 px/f. Start B's caption in the last 25% of the move and render with --blur.
- **Timing:** Pan on E.smooth over N = A.k x D / 34 f at depth 0.45, or A.k x D / 25 at 0.15-0.25: about 76 f for 2,600 px at k = 1, 106 f for 1,800 px at k = 2, 72 f for 1,800 px at k = 1. Dip on linear time, depth 0.15-0.45, its zoom rate peaking at 1-2.6%/f a quarter of the way in and out. Frame edge at most about 60 px/f. Beyond about 120 f, cut instead (cam-offframe-whip-relay or cam-punch-in-insert).
- **Use when:** Single-take and walkthrough films moving between two areas of one surface more than about a frame width apart (sidebar to canvas, one dashboard panel to another), where the viewer should see how they relate.
- **Avoid when:** Areas less than about a frame width apart (cam-reframe-to-subject), a cursor that should lead the move (cam-cursor-whip-orbit), or a wide view that is cluttered or unfinished, since the hop shows it.

### Base sinks away from the launching object

`dv-ground-falls-away` · camera · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

As an object launches (a send button, a card), the camera pushes slightly while the base it sat on drifts down and accelerates out of frame, so the object seems to lift off.

- **Build:** parallax with the base on its own layer and an E.buildIn drop. Anatomy: Camera push +2-4 %; base y on an ease-in to about 29 px/f; never settles. Sound: Kicks under it.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 58 f.
- **Use when:** The moment a request is sent; an object leaving its container.
- **Avoid when:** Moving the object itself fast at the same time.

### Breathing zoom between interactions

`cam-breathing-zoom` · camera · accent · energy calm · launch, feature, walkthrough

In a long act of several interactions in one framing, the camera pulls back after a reveal and lands, then makes one slow push that lands on the next interaction: two declared moves with a still beat between them, never a continuous breath.

- **Build:** Drive only k, from a keyframed zoom rate rather than from poses: rate(i) = interpolate(i, [s0, s0 + 72, s0 + 108, s0 + 168], [-0.0025, 0, 0.0014, 0.0011], {extrapolateLeft: 'clamp', extrapolateRight: 'clamp'}) with linear interpolation, and k = k0 * Math.exp(sum of rate(i) for i = s0..f), computed in a pure loop every frame with no state kept between renders. Put ax, ay on the element the next interaction touches, so the zoom pivots on it and it holds its screen position. Keyframe the rate so it crosses zero rather than resting there: |rate| may stay under 0.0002 for no more than 12 f. Close the act with a short exhale under the final hold: k x lmix(1, 0.94, prog(f, T, T + 60, E.out)).
- **Primitive:** `lib/handoff.creep`, `lib/handoff.intoCut`
- **Timing:** Pull after a reveal: -0.25%/f falling to 0 over 72 f (about -9% total). Push into the next interaction: 0 rising to +0.14%/f over 36 f, about +6% within 60 f of the zero crossing; table and list acts run +0.03 to +0.17%/f (about +6.6% total). Rate keyframes 36-90 f apart, linear. Exhale x0.94 over 60 f on E.out.
- **Use when:** Dashboard, analytics or table acts of 4-10 s with several interactions in one framing, where cutting would cost orientation; each move shows the next thing that changes.
- **Avoid when:** Shots shorter than about 90 f, acts that already move pose to pose with big pushes, or a scrolling feed (a zoom on a moving list reads as wobble).

### Composition jump-reframes on each arrival

`dv-jump-reframe-on-arrival` · camera · accent · energy high · launch, feature

While a collage is sparse, the whole composition jumps in one frame (about 180 px, or x1.11) each time an element arrives, holding 2-10 f between jumps.

- **Build:** collage({ camera }) steps on births (x1.05-1.11 or 150-200 px). Anatomy: Single-frame reframes on births; holds 2-10 f. Sound: None needed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Stepped`
- **Timing:** Holds 2-10 f.
- **Use when:** Stop-motion collage builds.
- **Avoid when:** Smooth films.

### Crane down with a delayed push

`cam-crane-push` · camera · accent · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

The camera tilts down the page past the chart to the detail cards while a slow push-in builds behind it, as if the operator were leaning in to read.

- **Build:** Sum two vertical components on the anchor camera's sy: a main move of about 240 px on prog(f, a, a + 64, E.smooth), and a 300 px drift on prog(f, a + 40, a + 220, E.rest) that overlaps it, so the motion never stalls and fades out slowly. Multiply k by lmix(1, 1.22, prog(f, a + 40, a + 240, E.rest)) so the push starts 40 f late and peaks while the tilt is decelerating. Put ax on the column the viewer will read so the push doesn't drift sideways.
- **Timing:** Main tilt 64 f on E.smooth, about 240 px, peak about 10 px/f mid-move. Drift 300 px from a + 40 to a + 220 on E.rest (peaks near 5.8 px/f, under 0.5 px/f by the end). Push +22% from a + 40 to a + 240 on E.rest, peak about +0.35%/f near a + 98.
- **Use when:** Moving down a long page or dashboard from the overview to the detail that matters.
- **Avoid when:** Pages too short to travel 500 px or more, or vertical formats where the push crops the column.

### Cursor-led whip orbit

`cam-cursor-whip-orbit` · camera · accent · energy high · walkthrough, feature, launch

Following a cursor that leads the way to the next panel, the camera swings fast across the product, yawing to show the slab's thick edge and rolling slightly.

- **Build:** Keyframe A (the current pose) and B, with ax, ay on the destination panel, yaw about +24 deg, roll about -10 deg and k = 0.77 x A.k, and blend lc(A, B, prog(f, a, a + 74, E.whip)) through camera(shot, 2400). Move the cursor in screen space along cursorArc(start, dest, prog(f, a - 5, a + 69, E.whip), 0.2), so it leads the camera by about 5 f and seems to drag it, projecting its destination with the same transform maths. Give the world container a 24-40 px side face (a darker tone of the surface, hinged on the right edge with rotateY(90deg)) so the yaw reveals the product's thickness. Render with --blur, since the peak is near 47 px/f.
- **Timing:** 74 f on E.whip, peak about 47 px/f at around 40% of the move. Yaw 0 -> 24 deg, roll 0 -> -10 deg, zoom x0.77. The cursor leads by 4-6 f.
- **Use when:** Moving between two distant panels of one product in a single-take or walkthrough film, where a cut would lose the spatial relationship.
- **Avoid when:** There is no cursor or other lead to motivate it (an unmotivated whip reads as a flourish), or the act already uses yaw for something else.

### Directional impact kick

`cam-impact-kick` · camera · accent · energy high · launch, sting, feature, vertical

On a true impact (a card landing, a lock-in, a slam) the whole frame jolts a few pixels in the direction of the hit and pushes a hair closer, then settles within a fifth of a second.

- **Build:** On the impact cue c, add a decaying jolt to the anchor camera: sx += dir.x * 8 * hitPulse(f - c, 1, 4) and sy += dir.y * 8 * hitPulse(f - c, 1, 4), where dir is the unit vector of the incoming object's travel, and multiply k by 1 + 0.015 * hitPulse(f - c, 2, 5). Take c from the contact frame in src/lib/sync.ts so sound and picture peak together, pair it with squash() on the landing object, and never add roll. Use it at most 2-3 times per film, and only where something truly lands.
- **Timing:** Jolt 6-10 px, attack 1 f, tau 4 f (gone in about 25 f). Push +1.5%, attack 2 f, tau 5 f. At most 2-3 per film.
- **Use when:** True landings and lock-ins: a heavy object slamming into a slot, or a statement locking together on a hit.
- **Avoid when:** Every beat or tick (that makes a shake, not a hit), soft UI arrivals, or mid camera move (it fights the move's ease).

### Living hold creep

`cam-living-hold` · camera · accent · energy calm · any

A long hold on one product state or the end card may keep a sub-pixel push or pull, one way, under 12 px/s at the frame's edge; most holds are simply still (the camera moves only with a purpose).

- **Build:** Set the anchor camera's ax, ay on the focal element so the creep pivots there. Multiply k by breath(prog(f, holdStart, holdEnd, E.linear) * (1 - nextMove), amount), where amount = 0.0005 x the hold length in frames and nextMove is the next move's 0..1 progress, so the next move releases the creep with no velocity step. Push on proof and result shots, pull (negative amount) on busy or chaotic boards, and use a tiny creep on the end card. For type or a single card, drift sideways instead: with g = f - holdStart, sx = sx0 - v * (g - 20 * (1 - Math.exp(-g / 20))), which leaves the seam at zero velocity and reaches v after about 60 f. Keep every layer the camera carries static inside the one transform, so nothing stair-steps on the pixel grid during the creep.
- **Primitive:** `lib/handoff.creep`, `lib/handoff.intoCut`
- **Timing:** Scale creep at most 0.02 %/f (about 1.2 %/s at 60 fps), pulls the same; end card 0.0125 %/f. Lateral creep at most 0.2 px/f@60 (12 px/s), one way. E.linear once at speed, with a 20 f exponential ease-in from a seam; released over the next move's own ease. Never a float that turns back.
- **Use when:** A long hold (2 s or more) on a product state or the end card where a barely visible push helps the read; never as idle life under every hold.
- **Avoid when:** Most holds: a still hold is fine. Never on a camera that already made its move in the shot, never stacked with another creep, never sideways back and forth.

### Masonry wall scrolls in, drifts, scrolls out

`dv-masonry-scroll` · camera · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A masonry of framed photo cards with words in the gaps scrolls up on an expo-out entry, decays to a slow drift, then leaves on a circ-in.

- **Build:** flickState with a short ramp, or a camera y on E.snapOut then E.launchIn. Anatomy: Entry 22 px/f with 72 % of the travel in the first 10 %; drift 0.7-0.9 px/f; exit circ-in. Sound: The bed.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Scroll`
- **Timing:** In 60 f, cruise, out 42 f.
- **Use when:** A wall of examples or use cases.
- **Avoid when:** Text inside the moving cards.

### Pull-back that turns into the cut

`cam-reversal-into-cut` · camera · accent · energy medium · launch, feature · also `dv-reversal-push`

A long, decelerating pull-back reveals the scene, comes to a stop, then turns into a short push that accelerates into the cut: anticipation for whatever comes next.

- **Build:** reversal({ from, start, pull, rest, push, fps }); cut on .cut (the push's last, fastest frame), .turn is the stop.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves.reversal`
- **Timing:** Pull to x0.85 (0.80-0.90) over 70 f on E.glideOut, or 2.5 s for a slow reveal; push +4 % (2-6 %) over 24 f on E.buildIn ending at its peak speed.
- **Use when:** The last cut of a film or an act; after a reveal that needs one more look.
- **Avoid when:** The next shot opens still: the push must hand its speed to something.

### Push-in with a roll swing

`cam-push-dutch-roll` · camera · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

The camera dives into one corner of the UI, rolls a few degrees off level mid-dive like a hand-steered move, and rolls back to level as it lands.

- **Build:** Blend lc(WIDE, TARGET, t) with t = prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth), where TARGET has ax, ay on the corner element, sx, sy at that element's current screen point (so it stays put while the frame grows around it) and k = 2.09 x WIDE.k. Add the roll on its own curve: roll = t < 0.57 ? mix(0, -4, E.smooth(t / 0.57)) : mix(-4, -0.3, E.smooth((t - 0.57) / 0.43)), passed as the Shot's roll so camera() keeps it rigid outside any tilt. For a tilted landing, ease pitch 0 -> 8 deg over the last 24 f. Keep |roll| under 11 deg.
- **Timing:** 60 f; zoom 1 -> 2.09 on E.smooth in log space, peak about 3.5%/f mid-move. Roll 0 -> -4 deg by 57% of the move, back to -0.3 deg at the end, each segment E.smooth. Optional pitch 0 -> 8 deg over the last 24 f.
- **Use when:** A push that would otherwise feel mechanical: diving into a settings corner, a sidebar or a detail panel.
- **Avoid when:** Next to another rolled or tilted move in the same act (one rotation axis per act), or on moves shorter than 40 f, where the roll reads as a wobble.

### Ring or field spins in and bleeds off

`dv-rotation-decay` · camera · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A ring of chips, a ring of tiles or a whole field of tiles arrives already turning and its rotation decays by a constant ratio to a slow cruise that never stops.

- **Build:** Build: rotationDecay(f, { start, w0: 8, ratio: 0.94, cruise: 0.5 }) (fx/Orbit, degrees and ratios per 60 fps frame): the ring arrives turning at w0 and bleeds off by the ratio to a cruise that never stops, closed form; <OrbitRing decay> draws the ring. Anatomy: Start 2.5-15 deg/f, decay x0.88-0.95 a frame, cruise 0.1-2.4 deg/f. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Orbit.rotationDecay`
- **Timing:** 30-100 f to the cruise.
- **Use when:** Integrations, sources, a galaxy of features around a centre.
- **Avoid when:** Rotation that stops dead.

### Dolly surge with a foreground pass

`cam-dolly-surge-foreground` · camera · signature · energy high · launch, sting

The camera surges from a wide shot into a 3x medium close-up, with most of the travel in half a second, and at the fastest moment a near object rushes past the lens before a long, slow creep.

- **Build:** Animate k = lmix(1, 3.1, prog(f, a, a + 67, E.smooth)) around the subject (or translateZ of a preserve-3d stage under perspective 2400px), multiplied by lmix(1, 1.04, prog(f, a + 47, a + 107, E.linear)) so the +4% creep starts 20 f before the push ends and the motion never stalls. Put one foreground object on its own layer above the world, 300-400 px off the anchor, and project it with a stronger scale, kFg = k ** 1.6 (screen position = sx + (p - ax) * kFg), so it grows and slides out past the frame edge around the push's peak frame (about a + 33); keep its crossing at 60-80 px/f or less. The motion-blur pass (--blur) streaks it, so never fake the streak with a CSS blur. Optional mid and far layers at 1.0x and 0.3x of the camera's translation add parallax.
- **Timing:** Push 67 f on E.smooth, zoom 1 -> 3.1, 10-90% of the travel in about 28 f, peak about 4.8%/f near a + 33. Creep +4% over 60 f on E.linear from a + 47. Foreground exits on the peak at 60-80 px/f or less, smeared by the blur pass.
- **Use when:** Opening a launch film into a 3D or layered world, or a sting that dives from an overview into the hero object.
- **Avoid when:** Flat UI with no depth layers (nothing to pass the lens), or calm walkthroughs.

### Fly-through of a depth field

`cam-z-field-flythrough` · camera · signature · energy high · launch, sting, feature

Dozens of flat screens or tokens float at different depths and the camera travels forward through them: near ones swell and slide off the frame edges, far ones barely drift, until the move lands square on one hero screen.

- **Build:** Seed 24-36 items with rand(i): x within +-2200 px, y within +-1300 px, z from 800 to 6000 px ahead of the start, keeping a 420 x 260 px corridor around the camera's path empty so nothing hits the lens head-on, and place the hero at (0, 0, Zh), sized in world px at the size it should read. Project each item yourself rather than through preserve-3d: with F = 1200 and d = z - camZ(f), draw it as a flat layer at translate(W/2 + (x - camX) x F/d, H/2 + (y - camY) x F/d) scale(F/d), z-ordered far to near, and unmount it once d < 300. Multiply each item's opacity by a far fade-in (0 -> 1 as d falls from 6000 to 4800) and by a speed gate, clamp((70 - v) / 20), where v is its screen travel since f - 1 (project it again with camZ(f - 1)), so whatever rushes past the lens dissolves instead of breaking the speed cap; sink distant items into the stage with an overlay of the stage colour at 0.5 x clamp((d - 1200) / 4000) instead of blurring 30 layers. For the dive, camZ = (Zh - F) x prog(f, a, a + N, E.cam) lands the hero at exactly scale 1, sharp and readable; for a breadth drift that ends in a cut, pull back 1200 px on E.out, cruise forward at 4 px/f with camY sinking 1.5 px/f, then ramp out over the last 18-24 f on E.contact and hard-cut on the fastest frame (tr-velocity-handoff-cut). Tokens may also turn slowly on rotateY (up to 10 deg/s each), and the whole move renders with --blur.
- **Timing:** Dive: 150-180 f on E.cam through 4,000 px of depth (Zh = 5200, F = 1200), landing the hero at scale 1 on the long settle. Drift: pull-back 40 f on E.out, cruise 90-120 f, exit ramp 18-24 f. Speed gate between 50 and 70 px/f; far fade over 1,200 px of depth; about 12-16 items on screen at once. The hero's copy starts once it moves under 20 px/f.
- **Use when:** Proving breadth (a whole platform, hundreds of templates, every integration) in 3-4 s without explaining any single screen; opening into a layered world; arriving on the one screen the next act is about.
- **Avoid when:** Items must be read in flight, there are fewer than about 15 of them (the field looks sparse), the film is flat with no depth language, or lc-swarm-cluster-burst already spends the film's breadth crescendo.

### Hero push with a 3D turn

`cam-hero-push-yaw` · camera · signature · energy high · launch, feature

From a wide view of the whole app, one continuous move pushes 2.5x into a single panel while yawing, so the panel turns toward the viewer and an empty side of the frame opens for the caption.

- **Build:** Build one scene on one world container with two Shots: WIDE (k = 1, flat) and HERO, with ax, ay on the panel centre, sx at 0.67 x width (0.33 for a panel on the left), k = 2.56, yaw 24-30 deg and pitch about 5 deg, rendered through camera(shot, 2400). Blend with lc(WIDE, HERO, prog(f, a, a + 60, E.smooth)); k already lerps in log space, so the push keeps an even perceived speed. Start the caption in the void at a + 45 (the last 25% of the move) so the word reveal and the camera settle read as one gesture, then keep the hold alive with breath(prog(f, a + 60, next, E.linear), 0.025) instead of a dead lock. Check that the panel's smallest meaningful text is at least 22 px on screen at k = 2.56, and render with --blur for the peak.
- **Timing:** 60 f on E.smooth, 10-90% of progress between 29% and 71% of the move, peak about 4.5%/f scale (around 47 px/f on screen) at 50%. Zoom 1 -> 2.56; yaw 0 -> 24-30 deg and pitch 0 -> 5 deg on the same curve. Caption starts at 75% of the move. Hold breath +2.5%.
- **Use when:** The film's energy peak: the one feature that needs both spatial orientation and close-up legibility, or a scene change inside a single-take film.
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film, or on a lone card with no surrounding app (the turn needs a world to orient against). Keep each act on its own rotation axis.

### Macro pan across giant type

`dv-macro-pan-type` · camera · signature · energy high · launch, sting

The camera slides across type so big it never fits the frame (half the frame height or more), fast at first and decaying, crisp in the centre and soft at the frame edges; a timeline can pan toward the past with speed swells.

- **Build:** camera x on E.snapOut over a single huge <Words>; edge softness as a static mask with two blur levels. Anatomy: Start 300+ px/f decaying about 1/t; edge softening; swells (185 px/f, 318 -> 20 -> 261...) while a tilt accelerates. Sound: Kicks on the cut and mid-pan; a stab at the end.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 29-62 f at 25-30 fps; 1881 px in 29 f.
- **Use when:** A giant number, a date line, a word as landscape.
- **Avoid when:** Text that must be read whole.

### Off-frame whip relay

`cam-offframe-whip-relay` · camera · signature · energy high · walkthrough, feature, launch

The cursor accelerates up and out of frame, the camera whips down the product while it's hidden, and the cursor re-enters from the top as a fast streak that brakes onto its target.

- **Build:** Three overlapping keyed parts. Cursor exit: y on E.in toward -10% of the frame height from a to a + 24, after which it stays off screen for 12 f. Camera: sy travels the product distance D (900-1400 px) on E.smooth over N = 2.86 x D / 75 frames (34-54 f), centred on a + 30 so its fastest stretch falls inside the hidden window and peaks at about 75 px/f. Cursor entry: from -10% to the target over 36 f from a + 36 on E.out, entering at about 63 px/f; while it moves faster than 12 px/f, draw a trailing rounded capsule behind the tip, 0.6 x speed long at 40% opacity, and let the blur pass handle the camera.
- **Timing:** Cursor exit 24 f on E.in (2.5 -> 15 px/f). Off screen 12 f. Camera 34-54 f on E.smooth centred on the hidden window, peak 60-75 px/f. Cursor re-enters at about 63 px/f and brakes over 36 f on E.out (speed ratio about 0.92 per frame).
- **Use when:** A big spatial jump within one product (top bar to bottom bar, one page to another) that should feel like a match-on-action without a cut.
- **Avoid when:** Films without a cursor, or destinations less than about one frame height away (a plain reframe is enough).

### Pull out from inside the object

`cam-inside-object-pullout` · camera · signature · energy medium · launch, sting, feature, vertical

The shot opens on what reads as a full-bleed colour field or a statement card, and one long pull reveals it was the face of a small object (an app icon, a card, a screen, the mark) sitting among its neighbours.

- **Build:** Lay the object out at true size inside its real context (a dock, a grid, a window, the lockup) in the anchor camera's world, with its face, corner radius and shadow as live layout in world units, never a bitmap. Shot FACE puts ax, ay on the object's centre at frame centre with k0 = 1.04 x max(W / objectW, H / objectH), so its edges sit just outside the frame (about 13.3 for a 144 px icon at 1920 wide), and Shot CONTEXT frames the object at k = 1 in its slot. Blend cam = lc(FACE, CONTEXT, prog(f, a, a + N, E.dolly)) with N = 25.7 x ln(k0); this caps the log zoom rate at about 6%/f mid-move, so anything entering at the frame corner moves under about 66 px/f, and the corners, the shadow and the neighbours arrive purely by coverage, with no fades of their own. Draw the opening copy on a screen-space overlay at toScreen(cam, centre), scaled by (cam.k / k0) ** 0.46 so it shrinks more slowly than the object, and fade it out on E.smooth while the object's on-screen width falls from 1.3x to 1.0x the copy's width, so it never spills past the edges. Read the face under a cam-living-hold creep before the pull, land with no overshoot, and start the next beat (an icon hop, a wordmark build) within 12 f of the settle.
- **Timing:** Face hold 24-48 f for the read, with a 0.04-0.07%/f creep. Pull from k0 = 8-14 to 1 over N = 25.7 x ln(k0) frames on E.dolly (about 53 f from 8x, 66 f from 13.3x), log rate peaking near 6%/f mid-move and landing at rest. Copy scale tracks k ** 0.46 and fades over the 8-14 f in which the object's width passes 1.3x -> 1.0x the copy width. Anchor travel to the slot under 10 px/f. --blur for frames above 12 px/f.
- **Use when:** Cold opens and hooks where a calm statement or a colour field should turn out to be part of the product (the question was printed on the app icon, the colour was one card in the grid); landing the mark into the final lockup; any reveal whose point is scale.
- **Avoid when:** The face is a photo or bitmap (it falls apart at 8-14x), the context it lands in is not recognisable at a glance, or a scale-through cut or detail-first pull-back has already used the same object. Once per film.

### Zoom into an object on a log curve

`dv-log-zoom-into-object` · camera · signature · energy medium · any

A point or a small object grows by 3-8x in log space (accelerating then decelerating, or decelerating from the start) and keeps going past frame fill, softening as it grows; an input box can enter barrel-distorted and straighten as it grows.

- **Build:** zoomThrough({ factor, frames, ease }) with lc() log blending. Anatomy: Scale on a log curve (tau about 7-15 f on the tail), slight roll 2.5 -> 0 deg/f; optional softening; barrel bulge for 6 f at the start. Sound: The fastest frame on a vocal sound or a glockenspiel note. Materials: The world is seen through a feathered porthole that opens faster than the footage zooms: the window grows about 7.6x (feathered 6 % of the radius) while the plate inside scales only about 1.9x, on twos with a few single-frame exceptions; the plate is a soft, deliberately upscaled frame.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Materials:** The world is seen through a feathered porthole that opens faster than the footage zooms: the window grows about 7.6x (feathered 6 % of the radius) while the plate inside scales only about 1.9x, on twos with a few single-frame exceptions; the plate is a soft, deliberately upscaled frame.
- **Timing:** 50-86 f for x3-8; peak 0.25 log/f.
- **Use when:** Dot to planet, a mark to a world, the prompt box becoming the stage.
- **Avoid when:** Linear scale (it reads as slowing down).

### Camera locks, the interface performs

`ps-locked-camera-holds` · pacing and structure · workhorse · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

After each move the camera stops dead, and for a 1-4 s read only the caption, the cursor and one micro-interaction move.

- **Build:** Between poses, blend with lc(A, B, E.cam(p)) from src/lib/camera.ts. At each pose, hold the Shot exactly: no breath(), scale constant, 0.0 px/f. Schedule events from the move's end so that no gap between visible changes exceeds 40 f: the UI action at moveEnd - 10 f, the caption word reveal (src/fx/Words.tsx) at moveEnd - 0.25 * moveDuration, cursor travel (src/fx/Cursor.tsx) on E.glide. Ambient life lives only in the background, for example a single-hue wash breathing ±3% opacity on a 240 f sine. The caption leaves as one block, opacity on E.smooth over 26-28 f with no stagger, and is gone 0-56 f before the next move starts.
- **Timing:** Holds 60-240 f (median about 150 f) at exactly 0 px/f; an in-frame event at least every 40 f; moves between holds 56-108 f E.cam; caption exit 26-28 f E.smooth, ending 0-56 f before the next move.
- **Use when:** Dense product UI that must be read, walkthroughs, and films where every move should feel deliberate because it contrasts with stillness.
- **Avoid when:** Kinetic type or fast montages where a dead camera reads as a stalled player, or holds with nothing in the UI to animate.

### One shot goes completely still

`dv-one-still-shot` · pacing and structure · accent · energy calm · any

After constant motion everywhere, one shot lands and holds completely still for half a second; the stillness becomes the emphasis.

- **Build:** A move on E.snapOut that ends exactly; then no creep for 28 f (declare the still range). Anatomy: Pull-out into the cut accelerating, the next shot opens still moving, then stops dead. Sound: A ding on the still frame.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Out 14 f, in 20 f, still 28 f.
- **Use when:** The keyword of the film ("Instantly").
- **Avoid when:** More than once per film; holds longer than about 30 f.

### Zoom energy decays shot by shot

`dv-shot-energy-decay` · pacing and structure · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

After a zoom transition, each following shot pushes in less than the one before (2.1 %/f, 0.54, 0.20, 0), so the sequence calms down without any shot being static.

- **Build:** Montage with push per shot decaying (MONTAGE ratio 0.3), or per-shot creep() rates from a decaying list. Anatomy: Per shot push rate times about 0.3. Sound: The bed thins with it.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Montage`
- **Timing:** Over 65 f of shots.
- **Use when:** The run of shots after a big transition.
- **Avoid when:** Reversing the order (it reads as random).

### Montage of constant-rate dolly-outs cut on snares

`dv-log-dolly-montage` · pacing and structure · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

A run of shots (billboards, posters, streets) each with a steady pull-back at a constant log rate, cut on snares, so the whole run reads as one continuous retreat.

- **Build:** <Montage> with one travel (pull) and cuts on the accent list. Anatomy: Same log rate in every shot; cuts within 45 ms of snares; the last shot longer. Sound: Cuts on snares.
- **Primitive:** `fx/Montage`
- **Timing:** Shots 25-50 f; final 85 f.
- **Use when:** Showing the product out in the world; the climax montage.
- **Avoid when:** Shots with different move directions.

### One camera journey

`ps-single-camera-journey` · pacing and structure · signature · energy calm · walkthrough, feature, launch

The film is one camera function: a punch-out opening, reframes across one large surface, a whip that swaps the copy on its peak, a snap zoom, a dive into an object and a reversal into the last cut; every cut is carried.

- **Build:** Write cam(f) once from punchOut, reframeChain, whip, snapZoomState, zoomThrough, handoffShot, reversal and scaleBreath (each move's output is a valid input to the next) and draw every shot through camera(cam(f)). One new camera idea per beat (1.5-2.5 s).
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** About 6 camera ideas in 10 s, one per beat; moves 27-126 f; holds never frozen (drift 30 px/s or creep 2-15 %/s).
- **Use when:** Walkthroughs of a single app, features where spatial orientation matters, and calm, premium product films.
- **Avoid when:** Multi-app or abstract stories, and films under 10 s.

### Camera orbits a panel in 3D

`dv-yaw-orbit` · depth and 3d · accent · energy medium · launch, feature

A floating panel or page turns in 3D (its far side receding, the yaw flipping), sometimes with a slight wide-lens bulge on a push; new content pops in during the tail.

- **Build:** Cards enterState lean on rotateY, or the camera's yaw in lib/camera.ts; barrel bow as a static SVG displacement map at two strengths. Anatomy: Yaw 2-8 deg (far side scaling 1 -> 0.85); a push of x1.57 with 3-5 % barrel bow; content pops in the tail. Sound: A level dip before the flash it leads into.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 34-54 f; 5 f ease-in, peak 45 px/f, long quart-out tail.
- **Use when:** Product screens that should feel like objects.
- **Avoid when:** Yaw beyond about 15 deg on readable UI.

### Object rises into frame as focus racks in

`dv-rise-focus-rack` · depth and 3d · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

A floating platform or object rises into frame, slowing, while the image racks from soft to sharp, the focus landing later than the position.

- **Build:** Cards enterState + RackFocus levels with the focus starting 4 f after the move. Anatomy: Rise 9 -> 2 px/f; focus lags by 20 f. Sound: None.
- **Primitive:** `fx/RackFocus`
- **Timing:** Rise 18 f; focus 40 f.
- **Use when:** Introducing a 3D object or a device.
- **Avoid when:** Racking before the move.

### Pull-back where the foreground lands first

`dv-parallax-landing-stagger` · depth and 3d · accent · energy calm · launch, feature

Opening on a button over a dot grid, the camera pulls back; the foreground lands about 10 frames before the background, so the depth reads from the timing alone.

- **Build:** parallax(layers with different frames) on one pull. Anatomy: Background on a soft-start ease-out (peak -5.5 %/f at f7) in log scale; foreground on a shorter curve. Sound: A glockenspiel-like note at 0.05 s.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** Background 58 f; foreground 38 f.
- **Use when:** Openers on a single object over a textured ground.
- **Avoid when:** Equal timing on both layers.

### Barrel-roll fly-in down a corridor

`dv-barrel-roll-flyin` · depth and 3d · signature · energy high · launch, sting

The camera rolls about 175 deg while flying down a corridor of light tiles to a hero object, pushing about 2x.

- **Build:** lib/camera roll + k on one ShotFn; tiles as a parallax field. Anatomy: Roll on a sine-out, push on an ease-in-out, light tiles passing. Sound: The music drops out.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Timing:** 72 f.
- **Use when:** The hero reveal of a 3D world, once.
- **Avoid when:** UI films; readable type during the roll.

### Camera tilt turns a flat graphic into a space

`dv-tilt-reveals-space` · depth and 3d · signature · energy medium · launch, sting

A flat column or ring becomes a perspective runway or a side-view carousel as the camera tilts; a grid ceiling or floor appears.

- **Build:** lib/camera pitch on a 3D-transformed container (perspective 1200 px). Anatomy: Tilt of 564 px or a swing from axial to side view; grid planes appear. Sound: Between beats. Materials: After the grid tips into a perspective floor, a minute paragraph lies on the floor beside an object, rotated and foreshortened with it and softened by the floor's depth of field: animate the camera, not the text.
- **Primitive:** `lib/camera-moves`
- **Materials:** After the grid tips into a perspective floor, a minute paragraph lies on the floor beside an object, rotated and foreshortened with it and softened by the floor's depth of field: animate the camera, not the text.
- **Timing:** 23-25 f in-out; then a constant orbit of 100 f.
- **Use when:** Moving from a flat 2D graphic into a 3D world.
- **Avoid when:** Without depth cues ready on the other side.
